artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Television Themes by Matt Berry, released in 2018 on Acid Jazz Records, is a genre-blending album that reimagines classic British television theme tunes through the lens of electronic, jazz, and rock. Featuring covers of iconic themes such as Doctor Who, Are You Being Served?, The Good Life, and Sorry!, the album showcases Berry’s signature lush arrangements, vintage synth textures, and a playful yet sophisticated approach to composition. The music balances nostalgic reverence with modern production, often transforming familiar melodies into atmospheric, instrumental pieces that evoke both retro charm and contemporary cool.

As Berry’s sixth studio album, Television Themes stands out in his discography for its accessible concept and broad appeal, marking his first UK Top 40 chart entry. While previous albums like Witchazel and The Small Hours leaned more toward psychedelic folk and introspective songwriting, this release highlights Berry’s versatility and deep appreciation for British pop culture. The album received positive critical attention for its inventive arrangements and nostalgic warmth, cementing Berry’s reputation as a distinctive voice in both comedy and music.
